title: Adaptive quota reserve miscalculation during concurrent route rebalance
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Our per-org adaptive quota reserve component sometimes computes an incorrect reserve when a route-level shard rebalance and autoscale event occur concurrently. The miscalculation results in either a transient over-allow (applications see more available tokens than they should) or duplicate reserve accounting that causes billing deltas and customer-reported unexplained credits. This ticket tracks investigation, mitigation, fix, and rollout for the issue.

What happened: The adaptive reserve algorithm periodically computes a small burst reserve based on recent request rate and a configurable headroom factor. During an autoscale-triggered route rebalance we observed that the reserve computation used inconsistent window metadata (mixing pre- and post-rebalance window sizes), leading to the reserve numerator being divided by a stale denominator. In practice this produced a reserve value that was 1.5x-3x larger than intended for short periods, and in a rare race produced a mirrored duplicate reserve entry when the rebind completed concurrently.

Symptoms observed:
- Short-lived surge of allowed requests from some orgs (~10-60s) with corresponding spike in downstream tokens consumed.
- Billing reconciliation shows small number (hundreds/day across fleet) of misattributed or duplicated charges.
- Trace logs show two reserve records for same (org,route) spanning the rebalance boundary in ~0.7% of rebalance events.
- Rate engine metrics: reserve_compute_time spiked and reserve_success_count deviated from historical.

Reproduction (dev env):
1) Start local rate-engine with deterministic shard rebind simulator (dev tool: shard-replay).
2) Configure a synthetic org with steady 200rps and reserve headroom 20%.
3) Trigger simulated autoscale that changes route window from 60s -> 30s and concurrently send a short burst.
4) Observe reserve entries in /metrics/reserves and logs: duplicated reserve id or reserve value > expected by >1.5x.

Logs (snippets):
- 2026-03-02T14:23:12Z [reserve] compute start org=org_231 window_size=60 prebound=true
- 2026-03-02T14:23:12Z [route_rebind] route=route-a shard=shard-17 window_new=30
- 2026-03-02T14:23:12Z [reserve] compute complete reserve_id=R_9f3 val=180 prewindow_den=60 postwindow_den=30
- 2026-03-02T14:23:13Z [reserve] apply failed duplicate-reserve-detected existing=R_9f3 new=R_9f3_dup

Initial hypothesis: Non-atomic read of window metadata combined with eventual consistency of the route metadata cache allowed reserve computation to use mixed-state inputs. The duplicate reserve arises because the reserve writer does not enforce a unique compare-and-swap keyed on the canonical reserve fingerprint; when metadata shifts mid-computation both writer paths can succeed.

Immediate mitigation done:
- Rolled out a hotfix to the metadata cache to short-circuit reserve computation if route metadata is flagged as "rebinding" (feature-gate: disable-adaptive-reserve-during-rebind). Deployed to canary (5% edge) on 2026-03-05.
- Added a temporary reconciliation job that scans reserves older than 30s and collapses duplicate reserve records into a single canonical entry while emitting an audit event for billing reconciliation.

Progress & next steps:
- Root-cause confirmed by replay and deterministic unit test (Luca).
- Design review completed with Kevin (runtime lead) and Maya (billing) on 2026-03-07. Outcome: implement atomic reserve writes and metadata-version-check in compute path.
- Proposed fix: compute reserve against a single metadata version token (metadata_version). During compute we read metadata_version once and include it in the reserve write; reserve write uses conditional compare-and-set on (org,route,metadata_version) to ensure only one succeeds. If CAS fails, recompute against latest metadata_version.
- Also adjust reserve formula to guard against division by small window sizes: clamp window_size minimum to 5s for reserve calc and use fractional fixed-point math to avoid integer truncation bias.

Implementation plan:
1) Add metadata_version read and include it in reserve payload (code: rate_engine/reserve.go).
2) Change reserve store to support CAS on composite key; add index on (org,route,metadata_version).
3) Add unit tests that simulate concurrent rebind and assert single reserve created.
4) Add integration test using shard-replay under load to validate no duplicate reserves across 10k rebind events.
5) Add e2e billing backfill runner that can idempotently heal duplicates in production for historical days.

Testing & validation:
- Unit tests: reserve_concurrent_rebind_test, reserve_window_clamp_test.
- Load test: 50k req/s synthetic orgs with random rebind schedule.
- Canary rollout: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% with monitoring gates on reserve_dup_rate, billing_delta, per-org allowance drift.

Rollout plan:
- Merge PR into release branch: runtime-1.20 (PR link in attachments).
- Canary to dedicated canary fleet for 24h, run reconciliation job for historic dup collapse, then broad rollout.
- Communication: send customer advisory to impacted orgs with summary and reconciliation window.

Monitoring: Add these dashboards/alerts:
- reserve_dup_rate (alert if >0.1% per hour per region)
- billing_delta_unexplained (alert if monthly extrapolated delta > $5000)
- reserve_compute_latency (alert if > p99 baseline * 3)
